classification.difficultyReason: Uses equally weighted letter selections, combines compulsory letters with excluded vowels and recognises the complementary at-least-one event.

content.prompt: Five-letter codes are formed from the letters of the word ALGORITHM. Find the probability that

answer.worked:
There are six consonants. Every five-letter selection has the same $5!$ arrangements, so this factor cancels from the probability.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{no vowels})&=\frac{\binom{6}{5}}{\binom{9}{5}}\\P(\text{no vowels})&=\frac{1}{21}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: at least one vowel is chosen.

answer.worked:
Use the complement of choosing no vowels.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one vowel})&=1-\frac{\binom{6}{5}}{\binom{9}{5}}\\P(\text{at least one vowel})&=\frac{20}{21}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the letters A and L are chosen.

answer.worked:
A and L are fixed in the selection. Choose the remaining three letters from the other seven.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{A and L chosen})&=\frac{\binom{7}{3}}{\binom{9}{5}}\\P(\text{A and L chosen})&=\frac{5}{18}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: the letters H and M are chosen, but no vowels are chosen.

answer.worked:
H and M are fixed. The remaining three letters must be chosen from the four other consonants L, G, R and T.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{H, M; no vowels})&=\frac{\binom{4}{3}}{\binom{9}{5}}\\P(\text{H, M; no vowels})&=\frac{2}{63}\end{align*}$$
